text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday it upgraded its rating on Petro-Canada's commercial paper and assigned a positive outlook to the integrated oil company's debentures and notes.
CBRS said it upgraded its rating on Petro-Canada's C$750 million commercial paper program to A-1, from a previous A-1 (low), with a stable outlook.
The company's senior long-term debt, which includes about C$1.3 billion of debentures and notes, continued to carry a A/Good Quality rating but the outlook was upped to positive.
CBRS said the rating changes followed an annual credit review and reflected the company's sold growth since 1994.
Petro-Canada is Canada's third-largest gas producer, fifth-largest oil producer and second-largest refiner and marketer.
It said Petro-Canada's earnings, balance sheet characteristics and risk measurement ratios have been favorable and easily met recommended benchmarks.
Its first half earnings this year were also buoyed by strong results in the upstream and downstream, unlike last year when oil price hedging affected earnings, CBRS said.

Petro-Canada has also maintained strong financial discipline, despite large commitments which have included Hibernia-related capital spending and its purchase of Amerada Hess Canada, the service said. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
